Vance's Own Analysis in '60 Minutes' Interview TV Elon Musk Is Portrayed on 'SNL': "The Worst Thing South Africa Has Ever Done"

The show also scored a two-year high in adults 18-49, with about 1.5 million viewers in that age range tuning in, and its best 18-34 rating in more than five years. NBC also says Saturday’s show was the most watched episode ever on Peacock, though it did not provide any numbers.

NBC also got big ratings in primetime Saturday with its telecast of Notre Dame’s 31-24 win over then No. 1 Miami in college football. The game averaged 9.1 million viewers on NBC and Peacock, making it the third most-watched primetime Notre Dame game since NBC and the university struck a broadcast deal in 1991. It was also easily the biggest game of NBC Sports’ primetime college football showcase (Big Ten or Notre Dame) so far this season.

The game led all college football telecasts for the weekend. The NBC-only portion of the game came in with about 8.6 million viewers, subject to adjustments as it started and finished outside the primetime window.

• 60 Minutes averaged 7.77 million viewers for Sunday’s edition, which featured a post-midterms interview with President Donald Trump. While it was the most watched primetime show of the week outside of live sports, it was also at the lower end of Trump’s appearances on the show since he declared his first run for president in 2015. He has been on 60 Minutes eight times since then, and Sunday’s show drew the second smallest audience of the eight behind an April 2026 interview.

• Along with a strong election night , last week’s evening network newscasts also drew larger than usual audiences. All three posted their best viewer numbers since February, with ABC’s World News Tonight at 9.14 million viewers, the NBC Nightly News at 7.27 million and the CBS Evening News at 4.33 million (not including retitled telecasts used to game the Nielsen system).

entertainment.title: ‘South Park’ Brings Back Tweek for First Time in 5 Years in Craig-Centric Episode
entertainment.summary: The penultimate episode of the "South America" season sent Tweek into club sports to spend more time with his boyfriend.
entertainment.body:
The six-episode 29th season of South Park ( or South America , this season ) is nearing the end of its run, and the penultimate episode, airing Wednesday night on Comedy Central , will spotlight an unsung and perhaps forgotten character, Craig Tucker, and bring back a fan favorite who has been missing from the season so far: his boyfriend, Tweek Tweak.

Season 29, episode five is titled “We Be Clubbin’,” and the logline, from a press release sent to The Hollywood Reporter on Wednesday morning, reads: “When club sports take over Craig’s afternoons and weekends, Tweek signs up to spend more time with him. Soon his whole family struggles to keep up.” Related Stories TV Streaming Ratings Take on a Halloween Vibe With 'Crystal Lake,' 'Carrie' TV 'South Park' Serves Up a Steaming Pile of Beef Satire -- and a 'GTA VI' Sneak Peek

Tweek, the over-caffeinated, paranoid wreck, has carved out a special spot in the hearts of South Park fans, but he hasn’t had a speaking role on the Comedy Central mainstay since the second episode of season 24, which aired in March 2021. If you forgot about Tweek, you likely forgot about Craig, too. He’s the show’s deadpan voice of reason, often calling out the four main characters for their antics in ways that double as meta-commentary on the show itself. Craig hasn’t stepped out of the background at South Park Elementary since 2019.

Still, Craig and Tweek have been together for more than a decade — at first, against their will. The two were paired off in the 2015 episode “Tweek x Craig,” in which the Asian girls at school start drawing yaoi art of them in affectionate and homoerotic poses. A desperate-to-seem-woke Randy Marsh decides that people don’t choose to be gay; “Asians decide,” or, as he later clarifies, “the Japanese.” The boys try to stop the frenzy by staging a breakup, then end up playing along as a couple. In the end, it stuck, and the relationship is now South Park canon.

It’s unclear whether or how the episode will tie into the season’s running threads: the town’s name Trump-era name update to South America and the change coming in November with the Nov. 19 release of Grand Theft Auto VI , a gag widely read as a nod to the just-passed midterm elections. South Park will most likely find a way. Or maybe, as Tweek would scream, “That’s too much pressure!”

South Park season 29, episode 5, “We Be Clubbin’,” airs at 10 p.m. ET/PT on Comedy Central and streams on Paramount+ starting Thursday.

entertainment.title: 10 Years Ago Beyoncé and the Chicks Performed at the CMA Awards. It’s Still Making Waves
entertainment.summary: The controversy that followed their collab on "Daddy Lessons" in Nashville was an experience that deeply impacted the Cowboy Carter singer
entertainment.body:
A decade ago this month, the 50th CMA Awards booked one of the most talked about, and arguably one of the most powerful, performances in the history of broadcast . Alongside a New Orleans second-line style band, Beyoncé joined the Chicks for a rendition of her track “Daddy Lessons” — which featured an interpolation of the country trio’s “Long Time Gone” — off her masterpiece Lemonade .

Ten years later, the performance’s impact still reverberates, and so does the impression that the country music industry left on Beyoncé, the most awarded musician in Grammy history.

It was an electric performance for many overt reasons, but especially for two stories happening behind the scenes: “Daddy Lessons” was about to be deemed ineligible for contention in the country categories at the Grammy Awards by the Recording Academy; and the Chicks hadn’t appeared on the CMA broadcast since they were expunged from the country music industry in 2003. With the banjo and fiddle on high and the foursome hard stamping their Lone Star roots with proclamations of “Texas!” the collab should have screamed “country” to anyone watching. Instead, it resulted in a sour experience that led to Beyoncé making Act II: Cowboy Carter , her exploration and reclaiming of American roots traditions.

Much was made of how Beyoncé introduced that now Grammy-winning body of work: posting on Instagram that Cowboy Carter “ain’t a Country album. This is a ‘Beyoncé’ album.” But why would she claim a genre that wouldn’t claim her?

Controversy, if you can call it that, followed the performance. Alan Jackson reportedly walked out, and cameras captured some stone-cold faces in the crowd. Many argued that Beyoncé — singing a murder ballad that mentions the Second Amendment, no less — wasn’t country enough. But that wasn’t exactly a solid case to make when the genre, and the awards, openly embraced plenty of white pop collaborations. Just the year before, Justin Timberlake joined Chris Stapleton for a show-stopping highlight , and since then everyone from Katy Perry to Post Malone have taken the stage. entertainment.title: Solana Joins Sony’s Since ’93 Records as Label Expands African Talent Roster
entertainment.summary: The 23-year-old Lagos-born singer dropped her breakthrough track "Okunkun" earlier this year.
entertainment.body:
Lagos-born singer Solana has signed with Since ’93 records, the label and management group has revealed exclusively to Billboard U.K .

The deal sees the emerging Nigerian artist join the U.K.-based company, which has also been home to African artists including Tems and Tyla . Solana is developing ‘YoruPop,’ a sound combining the Yoruba language and influences with synth-pop, Fuji music, R&B and electronic production.

Solana’s signing aligns with the release of her debut EP, Girl From The West , due this Friday (Nov. 13). The 23-year-old dropped her breakthrough single “Okunkun” (translating to “darkness” in Yoruba) earlier this year and has since received co-signs across social media from the likes of SZA , Tyla , Doechii and Little Simz . She has also been named a Spotify EQUAL Africa Ambassador.

“Super excited to partner with Since ‘93 and the Sony Music team for this next chapter,” Solana said in a press statement. “Thank you to all my lanterns for your support, we’re bringing the world into our YoruPop universe. I’m excited to share my world with you, Girl From The West.”

Riki Bleau , co-president of Since ‘93, added, “We are excited to announce the Queen of YoruPop, Solana, as a new signing to Since ’93, continuing a rich tradition of supporting exceptional female talent from Africa like Tems and Tyla.”

Since ‘93 began as Avant Garde Music in 2012, founded by Bleau. It focused on artist management and music publishing working with Emeli Sandé , Labrinth and Sam Smith , among others. In 2018, the firm relaunched as a new label with Sony Music , with early signings including the BRIT-winning rapper Aitch and Fredo , who scored a No. 5 mixtape on the Official U.K. Albums Chart with Tables Turn later that year.

The current Since ‘93 roster includes Cat Burns — who enjoyed a star turn on BBC’s The Celebrity Traitors last year alongside releasing her second LP, How To Be Human — alongside the Elton John -backed songwriter Nectar Woode , and Shallipopi , a singer and rapper from Nigeria.

In recognition of his tenure at Since ‘93, where he serves alongside fellow co-president Glen Aitkins , Bleau was named to Billboard ’s 2026 Global Power Players List . Speaking about the honor , he said, “I’m grateful to Billboard for this recognition and to be among so many incredible ‘doers’ from our industry.

entertainment.title: Frankie Muniz explains how he avoided infamous child star downfall and details ‘roller coaster of emotions’ of racing career
entertainment.summary: Muniz's past co-stars include Amanda Bynes and the late Hayden Panettiere.
entertainment.body:
Frankie Muniz was able to avoid the infamous child star downfall, going from successful actor to accomplished race car driver over the course of his decades-long career.

Muniz, who was just 13 years old when he began filming the hit sitcom “Malcolm in the Middle,” attributes that to “never” caring about “fame.”

“I think a lot of people who get into the business or find popularity or fame or whatever it may be — success at a young age — you expect it to continue,” the 40-year-old told Page Six in an exclusive interview ahead of Wednesday’s Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic, a first-of-its-kind night of racing and music honoring service members at Florida’s Daytona International Speedway.

“You expect it to always be there. And as that starts to go away, as the phone rings less and less, I feel like that’s shocking, like that rejection or the feeling of rejection is shocking for a lot of people to take. And maybe they go and look for something else to fill that void or fill that feeling that they are being wanted or needed or admired.”

Muniz, whose past co-stars have included Amanda Bynes and the late Hayden Panettiere , insisted he “never necessarily cared about” that feeling.

“I don’t care if people like me,” he added. “I’m just me. And I’m doing what I want to do. I just so happen to go from being an actor on a TV show to racing cars.”

And in between, he was involved with a few different musical groups as both a drummer and manager before acquiring and selling an olive oil company with his recently estranged wife, Paige Price .

entertainment.title: Jane Seymour shares the story behind her ‘unique’ engagement ring from fiancé John Zambetti: ‘It spoke to him’
entertainment.summary: Plus, how the antique sparkler inspired her new jewelry collection for QVC.
entertainment.body:
Jane Seymour announced her engagement to musician John Zambetti this summer, and the English actress’ antique two-stone diamond ring is steeped in symbolism.

“[John] had seen it, I think, in a vintage stall somewhere at an art show. And it spoke to him, and he went, ‘That’s what I want to give Jane when the time’s right,'” Seymour, 75, told Page Six Style, quipping, “Who knew I’d find love at this time in my life?”

“It’s called a ‘toi et moi’ ring, and apparently Napoleon presented one to Josephine back in the day. I had no idea!”

The Emmy and Golden Globe winner’s “unique” Victorian-era sparkler features a floral motif, and she found the placement of the dual center stones (representing herself and her husband-to-be) especially meaningful.

“We are together, we’re connected, we’re not on top of one another, we’re equally side by side, we are aligned,” she explained, adding that “his past and my past” are symbolized by the smaller diamonds along the band.

“I think the sentiment behind it as well was that … you connect with someone, and you’ve had a life. You bring whatever you call it, baggage or experience or the spirit of your journey in life. And it’s never too late.”

The “Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman” star was so inspired by the one-of-a-kind ring, in fact, that it informed her latest Jane Seymour Designs jewelry collection for QVC, composed of two-stone rings, necklaces, bracelets and earrings.

“I called it Soul to Soul because I think more than anything, we want to connect right now. And that’s what’s missing in today’s society and especially amongst young people, with the texts and the Instagrams and social media,” Seymour said.

After the VisionQuest finale reunited Vision ( Paul Bettany ) and sons Tommy Maximoff ( Ruaridh Mollica ) and Billy Maximoff ( Joe Locke ) to defeat a grieving Ultron ( James Spader ) from his attempt to wipe out humanity, Wanda Maximoff ( Elizabeth Olsen ) teased her return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

The second post-credit scene from the Nov. 11 episode begins with a flashback to Wanda, a.k.a. the Scarlet Witch—who was drowning in grief and corrupted by the Darkhold's dark magic after losing Vision and her sons in WandaVision —burying herself in rubble at the end of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness .

Her moment of redemption followed the wake of destruction after she tried to kidnap another version of her sons—who disappeared after she let go of her projected version of Westview—when she brought down the temple at Mount Wundagore, wiping out every copy of the Darkhold across the multiverse.

But Dr. Doom ( Robert Downey Jr. ) has other plans for Wanda. As he lifted debris from her lifeless body, he proclaimed, "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine."

Worlds collide in Doomsday —premiering Dec. 18—with many of the OG Avengers (minus Downey's late Iron Man), Black Panther 's Wakandans, the Fantastic Four and the X-Men uniting to face Dr. Doom's existential threat to the multiverse.

entertainment.body:
Dianna Russini’s big return to TV ran into a disastrous hurdle when the debut of her new BetUS show, “The Russini Report,” was delayed by more than 10 minutes.

The embattled sports reporter was meant to make her highly anticipated return Wednesday morning, months after her bombshell scandal with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel derailed her career at the New York Times-owned Athletic.

The show was meant to premiere at 12 p.m. ET, but by 12:15 p.m., it still had not aired.

Production sources exclusively tell Page Six that the delay was due to an overwhelming number of viewers, adding that BetUS was “working on adding capacity, as it’s the record number of views on their site.”

BetUS later confirmed that when they tweeted, “Well… you broke it. 😅 The premiere of The Russini Report drew a record-breaking audience today! We’re adding more seats so everyone gets in. Stay with us! We’ll be back shortly. 🙏.”

On X, many users vented their frustration , complaining that the link did not work.

“Doesn’t work. Oh how the mighty have fallen,” one X user wrote.

“Probably wasn’t even more than a thousand people and the server crashed,” someone else typed.

Usher and Chris Brown have canceled another pair of shows on their extended R&B Tour. As of Wednesday (Nov. 11), Ticketmaster displayed cancelation notices for Nov. 16 in Los Angeles at SoFi Stadium and the Dec. 6 date at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami. entertainment.body:
In her first conversation about her participation in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim new documentary about Elizabeth Holmes , You Can See Everything , The Dropout alum revealed she signed onto the project without consulting her team.

“When you said you had 90 minutes of footage for me to see and help you work through, I was like, ‘Oh, he just wants some advice,’” Seyfried recalled of her earliest conversations with Fielder—with whom she was connected through Emma Stone —in a joint interview alongside Oppenheim for Rolling Stone published Nov. 11. “He just wants us to know about my experience playing her and researching her and going into the mind of that quote-unquote character I portrayed.’”

However, while Seyfried had previously said she’d never portray the disgraced Theranos founder after the limited series, Fielder and Oppenheim’s film, which released in theaters in early November, was too inspiring to pass up.

“After the Zoom, I was totally game to do whatever you needed,” she continued. “It was just your energy [that persuaded me], and how much time you had spent [on this project], and that nobody knew this was happening .”

But while Fielder has earned a reputation for truly shocking projects, Seyfried “wasn’t nervous” to work with The Rehearsal creator.

“There was no protection,” the 40-year-old—who acknowledged she had to remind herself to put on mascara before they began filming for the first time—continued. “There was no advocate for me. I just felt like I was totally game because I was so invested in what you were doing and already had this strange level of trust in you guys.”

Still, Seyfried admitted that as her involvement in the project grew—the Mean Girls alum ended up participating in reenactments as Holmes alongside Christopher Abbott , who played Holmes’ husband Billy Evans , as well as appearing as herself—she weighed “a lot of risk” in her mind.

In fact, Fielder emphasized that Seyfried had “no approval” over the scripts or dialogue in the film to ensure its documentary standard.

entertainment.title: First Look at the Kids’ Choice Awards 2026 Set Design: “We Really Tried to Create a Huge Playground” (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: Set designer Florian Wieder and Nickelodeon's Paul Medford talk about how the show will be different this year — its first time airing on CBS — and tease how that signature slime will be incorporated.
entertainment.body:
Kids’ Choice Awards set designer Florian Wieder promises that this year’s show will have lots of surprises — and, of course, lots of slime.

The Emmy-winning producer and production designer is reluctant to spill too many details and ruin the surprise for viewers, but he shares that many elements of the set are designed to do something interactive, which is where the slime comes in. For example, this year’s set will feature a swing and a slide that both have slime elements. (There also is a squirrel with laser beams coming out of its eyes.) “[The slime is] mostly hidden, of course, so you don’t know what to expect,” he says. “That’s the point. It’s never just, OK, you’re just sliming people. It’s always attached to something, to make it a little bit more interesting rather than just [spewing slime] around.” Related Stories TV Skye From 'Paw Patrol' Is Getting Her Own Spinoff TV CBS Unveils Competitors for Drew Barrymore-Hosted 'Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic' Special (Exclusive)

Wieder, whose credits also include serving as designer for the MTV Video Music Awards, the Eurovision Song Contest and the upcoming Grammys, has also worked with artists including Beyoncé, Adele, Jennifer Lopez, U2 and Lady Gaga. But he’s also no stranger to the Kids’ Choice Awards, having worked on the show previously. “You actually get a proper understanding of the show’s DNA and what this show is about,” he says. “But on the other hand, we always try to come up with something that feels new and fresh. The show has to reinvent every year; otherwise, it’s not a surprise anymore.”

He adds that the Kids’ Choice Awards is one of his favorite shows to work on. “We all feel like we get beamed back into our childhood because we’re allowed to be so creative and do all the crazy stuff,” he says, noting that it’s a collaborative process between him and his team, the network and the producers. “Everybody throws ideas on the table. We really tried to create a huge playground, with all the Nickelodeon DNA, and that’s what led us through this entire creative process.”

Paul Medford, vp live-action unscripted kids and family at Nickelodeon, echoes that sentiment. “This year, we’re taking everything fans love about the Kids’ Choice Awards and making it even bigger,” he says. “Our theme is ‘Everyone’s a Kid at Heart,’ which is really about reminding everyone that no matter your age, there’s always a kid in you who loves to have fun, laugh and let loose.”

entertainment.title: Taylor Swift Will Be Honored With The Hollywood Reporter’s Sherry Lansing Leadership Award at Women in Entertainment Gala
entertainment.summary: Greta Gerwig will bestow the honor to her at the event, which is presented by founding sponsor Lifetime and title sponsor Lilly.
entertainment.body:
The Hollywood Reporter announced Wednesday that Taylor Swift will receive this year’s prestigious Sherry Lansing Leadership Award during its annual Women in Entertainment breakfast gala in Los Angeles. Attended by 600 industry leaders and VIPs, the magazine’s beloved marquee event coincides with the release of The Hollywood Reporter ’s Women in Entertainment issue, featuring the highly anticipated Power 100, a list of the most powerful female executives and talent in entertainment. Greta Gerwig will give the award to Taylor Swift at the gala, which is presented by founding sponsor Lifetime and title sponsor Lilly.

The Sherry Lansing Leadership Award recognizes trailblazers and philanthropists in entertainment and media and was established in honor of Sherry Lansing, the first woman to head a Hollywood studio (Lansing is the former CEO of Paramount Pictures). Past recipients of this honor include Gwyneth Paltrow, Adele, Charlize Theron, Reese Witherspoon, Viola Davis, Barbra Streisand, Shonda Rhimes, Oprah Winfrey, Diane Keaton and Meryl Streep.

“Taylor Swift took on an industry that has long underestimated women and won on every front: artistically, commercially and on the question of who owns her work,” said THR editor-in-chief Maer Roshan. “She reclaimed her catalog, set new terms for the artists who follow her and became the most popular musician in the world while doing it — and helping scores of other artists along the way. We’re proud to honor her with the Sherry Lansing Leadership Award.”

“I am so pleased to recognize Taylor Swift with the award that bears my name,” Sherry Lansing said. “She has paved the way for women in music, demonstrating what is possible when a woman takes ownership of her work, her career and her future. Equally impressive is her generosity and commitment to giving back. She is an extraordinary talent and a remarkable role model, and I could not be more proud to see her receive this award.”

Gerwig is a four-time Oscar-nominated director, writer and actor. Her global phenomenon Barbie , which she directed and co-wrote, established her as one of the most commercially successful filmmakers working today. The film earned eight Oscar nominations, including best picture and best adapted screenplay, and won for best original song. Her solo directorial debut, Lady Bird , earned her Oscar nominations for directing and original screenplay, and her adaptation of Little Women received six Oscar nominations, including best picture and best adapted screenplay. In front of the camera, Gerwig earned a Golden Globe nomination for Frances Ha , which she co-wrote with Noah Baumbach. Other notable credits include Greenberg, Lola Versus, Mistress America (also co-written with Baumbach), Maggie’s Plan, Jackie, 20th Century Women, White Noise and Jay Kelly.

entertainment.title: How The Rings Of Power In The Prime Video Series Differ From The Lord Of The Rings Books
entertainment.summary: Season 3 of The Rings of Power puts its magic rings front and center, but how close is the show to Tolkien's version? Here's how the two compare.
entertainment.body:
Ben Rothstein/Prime Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Warning: Spoilers for "The Rings of Power" Season 3 ahead!

Season 3 of "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" premiered with a bang. Four episodes (half the season) dropped all at once, and the Season 3 storyline (which is functioning as a kind of soft reboot for the series) dives right into the action of the War of the Elves and Sauron . A big part of the drama focuses on the Rings of Power themselves. We see characters like Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), Gil-galad (Benjamin Walker), and even Theo (Tyroe Muhafidin) wielding their overpowered jewelry to heal wounds, receive visions, and dominate in battle.

But is that what the Rings of Power actually look like in Tolkien's original source material? Not exactly. The kind of magic we're seeing people wield in "The Rings of Power" is more defined. It's closer to what fans of the fantasy genre might call hard magic. That means the magic operates under a defined system with rules and limitations. The magic in "The Rings of Power" isn't quite as strict as it can get. But in contrast, Tolkien's writings around the Rings of Power lean more toward a soft magic system that doesn't get bogged down in the details.

There's also the fact that written story form always leaves more to the imagination. When you adapt a written story to the screen, you need to depict certain things that can remain unexplained on the page.

Ben Rothstein/Prime Showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay have spent two seasons introducing the majority of the show's titular jewelry. The Season 1 finale gave us the Elven Rings (a sequence that was already out of order from the Tolkien timeline). By the time the Season 2 ending arrived, we also had the seven Rings for the Dwarves and the nine for Mortal Men doomed to die. That just leaves the One Ring to rule them all — which Payne and McKay have confirmed we'll get in Season 3 (although four episodes in, Sauron is still struggling to figure out the magic sauce to get that job done).

Each race's Rings of Power in the show are doing different things. The Elven Rings are empowering their wearers to literally heal wounds and grant them visions. The Dwarven Rings haven't been worn as much — especially with King Durin IV (Owain Arthur) wisely hiding them. But we saw enough in Season 2 to know they corrupt their wearers. We also saw King Durin III (Peter Mullan) use one of the Rings like a sort of water stick to figure out where to dig to open up shafts of light.

entertainment.title: Angie Martinez’s Unaired Tupac Shakur Interview Set for Release After 30 Years
entertainment.summary: The radio personality who spent 28 years at New York's Hot 97 will host Netflix's The Tupac Tapes , a four-part podcast series premiering Nov. 27
entertainment.body:
In 1996, New York radio personality Angie Martinez flew to Los Angeles for an interview with Tupac Shakur . The conversation originated with the rapper, who suggested it be hosted in his home. There were some things he wanted to get off of his chest. Some parts of the conversation made Martinez feel uneasy at the thought of airing them, so she shared select segments but kept most of the conversation buried at the time. A few months later, Shakur was murdered . Now, Martinez is brushing the dust off of one of the rapper’s final interviews with The Tupac Tapes .

The four-part podcast series hosted by Martinez will premiere Nov. 27 on Netflix . It will mark the first time her complete interview with Shakur is heard by the public, 30 years after it took place. “There were things said in that conversation that could have hurt people, damaged relationships, and added fuel to an already dangerous situation,” Martinez told Tudum . “I chose not to release the more inflammatory parts. After Pac died, it became even more complicated. I felt a responsibility to protect something that was never meant to become his final statement.”

Martinez began her career at Hot 97, a staple in New York media. The parts of the interview she did air at the time spotlighted Shakur’s insistence that, despite what the hip-hop landscape might have suggested at the time, he wasn’t at war with the entire East Coast. The official trailer for The Tupac Tapes offers a glimpse into the parts that were omitted.

“I’ve done more for credibility in hip-hop than any fucking artist,” Shakur says in one clip. In another, he pushes back on Martinez, who’d started to say there were people who showed him love, before the rapper cut her off. “Where’s the fucking love?” he asked. “Just because they didn’t kill me? What love?”

When Shakur was killed shortly after, at the age of 25, Martinez was on shift at the station and shared the news on air. “It was one of the most emotional moments of my career,” she said. “I think about that whenever I think about the real human cost of everything that was happening. More than anything, I hope people leave with a greater sense of empathy. Because behind all the headlines, the records, the rivalries, and the mythology, there were real people. entertainment.title: The Rings Of Power Season 3 Episode 2 Delivers A Shocking Death No One Saw Coming
entertainment.summary: "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3 has killed off a character we all thought was here for the long run.
entertainment.body:
Prime Video Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 2 - "The Gift of Men"

"The Rings of Power" Season 3 jumps forward in time five years. This creates the feeling of a soft reboot , as the landscape has changed a lot in that time. This plays into an unexpected departure at the end of Season 3, Episode 2: Eärien's sudden death is a real shocker. Ema Horvath's Númenórean character played a substantial role in the first two seasons, and, up until the Season 3 premiere, it felt like her importance was only going to increase.

It's important to point out that Horvath's character was entirely made up for the show, so there is no specific path that she needed to go down in terms of Tolkien's source material. However, as a member of one of the most influential Human families in Middle-earth history, many likely assumed that she would continue to play an important part in the story. When Season 3 Episode 2 ends and she's suddenly gone, it comes as quite the shock for those who watched the previous two seasons.

The character's dramatic ending is as shocking as it is unexpected. Throughout Episode 2, Eärien is revealed as a covert member of the Faithful (the pro-Elvish faction of Humans on the island nation of Númenor). She's deeply ensconced in the inner circle of her enemies — until she's discovered and trapped in the final minutes of the episode. With nowhere to go, Eärien steps up to a balcony and casts herself onto the road below. It's the stuff of legend, and it sounds Tolkienian enough. But it really does come out of left field, especially considering where we left the character a season ago.

Prime Video In Tolkien's original writings, there's a distinct lack of female representation in Eärien's family. All we hear about are her dad, Elendil (Lloyd Owen), her brother, Isildur (Maxim Baldry), and her other brother, Anárion (Andrew Richardson). Elendil's wife is never mentioned, nor is it stated that he has any other children. Showrunners JD Payne and Patrick McKay (who have spoken out about the backlash to "The Rings of Power" ) filled the female gap with Eärien, who got a solid amount of screen time across Season 1 and Season 2.

Eärien started as the innocent and wide-eyed "baby" of the family. While her father and brothers leaned toward pro-Elvish sympathies, Eärien was attracted to the anti-Elvish group called the King's Men. This is led by Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle), who, by the end of Season 2, has usurped the throne and started forming a ring of trusted advisors to help him rule. The last we saw of her in Season 2, Eärien was on the edge of that circle and clearly interested in getting more involved.

entertainment.title: Rock Hall of Fame 2026 Induction Ceremony: Who Is and Isn’t Attending
entertainment.summary: Saturday's (Nov. 14) celebration at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles will be missing quite a few bold-faced names.
entertainment.body:
Saturday’s (Nov. 14) 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction might set a new high-water mark for low attendance among A-list guests of honor. While the annual gathering celebrating the latest names to be etched on the wall at the Cleveland museum regularly features a few no-shows — due to lingering inter-band tensions, health and scheduling issues or, in some cases, contempt for the whole exercise — this year’s event looks like it will have empty seats for more than half the living honorees.

Though the Hall of Fame has not officially confirmed who will, or won’t, be on hand, some acts have taken the initiative to confirm their absence in advance.

It’s no surprise that Oasis ‘ Noel and Liam Gallagher seem unlikely to make the flight for their induction after making the ballot three years in a row given their past statements about the Rock Hall. While spokespeople for the Britpop legends have not returned Billboard ‘s request for comment on their plans, singer Liam Gallagher has made it pretty clear in recent X comments that he’s staying put.

“It’s too far to be going for the night I got s–t to do it’s Christmas,” he wrote on Tuesday morning (Nov. 10) in response to a report that Oasis are not going to be in the house. In addition, guitarist/songwriter Noel Gallagher has booked his first solo gig since Oasis’ 2025 reunion tour with an appearance at Goldie’s EFG Jazz Festival in London, also on Saturday. Liam doubled-down on his no-show plans in a follow-up tweet on Tuesday in response to a fan who noted that “not many artists” show up to the affair, writing , “If it was in the UK I’d be there but for some reason it’s in LA and that’s miles.”

Also on Tuesday, Sade , said they will not make the trip. The elusive British act fronted by singer Sade Adu , confirmed the news in a post , writing, “Sorry we can’t be there in person to celebrate with the other artists. Please know that our absence takes nothing away from how much this recognition means to us.”

After landing in the Hall on their third try, Iron Maiden won’t be on hand due to a scheduling conflict with their Australian tour. The British heavy metal giants kicked off their run of Run For Your Lives world tour shows in Australia on Wednesday (Nov. 11) at Adelaide Entertainment Centre, with follow-up shows booked for Friday (Nov. 13) and Sunday (Nov. 15), making the nearly 8,000-mile trip an impossibility.

Plus, for the record, singer Bruce Dickinson referred to the RRHOF as an “ utter and complete load of bollocks ” in 2018, 13 years after the band first became eligible for induction.

entertainment.title: Benson Boone Set to Perform at NHL’s 2027 Winter Classic in Salt Lake City (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: The Utah Mammoth is set to host the Colorado Avalanche in the latest edition of the annual outdoor game, taking place at Rice Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City.
entertainment.body:
Benson Boone is set to headline the entertainment portion of the National Hockey League’s 2027 Discover Winter Classic, The Hollywood Reporter has exclusively learned.

The annual outdoor hockey game is scheduled for New Year’s Eve in Salt Lake City, Utah. The Utah Mammoth, who joined the league as an expansion team in 2024, will host their first-ever edition of the Winter Classic at Rice Eccles Stadium against the Colorado Avalanche. The Mammoth become the 32nd NHL franchise to participate in the outdoor event — a regular-season game for the teams. Related Stories TV Where to Watch the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race Live Online Business Bob Iger's Son to Call Games for Lakers G League Team

Boone, fresh off his Wanted Man tour, is set to perform during the first intermission of the game during a performance presented by Ticketmaster, according to a release. The pop star is known for his energetic performances, which often include a flip — or two. The 24-year-old broke out with his chart-topping single “Beautiful Things,” which helped earn him a best new artist nomination at the 2025 Grammy Awards.

“The Winter Classic is always about creating something unforgettable, and this year we’re taking that to another level. We’re turning the stadium into a true winter wonderland, and Benson Boone is the perfect artist to bring it to life,” NHL president of events and content Steve Mayer said in a statement. “He’s an incredible performer with a real sense of showmanship, and we can’t wait to see what he does on this stage to create a memorable experience for the fans in the stadium and everyone tuning in from home.”

The NHL recently had a slew of musical acts perform during the first intermission of the recent Heritage Classic, which took place at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg, Manitoba, at the end of October. The matchup featured two Canadian teams, the Winnipeg Jets and the Montreal Canadiens.

Off Campus star Ella Bright hosted the Heritage Classic intermission show. The musical acts — Remi Wolf, Wolf Parade, Feist and G Flip — were an homage to Heated Rivalry and Off Campus , the two popular hockey romance shows that dominated pop culture over the last year.

The Discover NHL Winter Classic will air on TNT, HBO Max and TruTV in the U.S and TVAS in Canada beginning at 4 p.m. Mountain Time. Tickets to the game are available through Ticketmaster .

entertainment.title: Iceland Airwaves’ 2026 Edition Ditched Headliners in Major Shake-Up: ‘If You’re Not Evolving, You’ll Just Die and Wither’
entertainment.summary: The tastemaking festival and conference returned to Reykjavík last week (Nov. 4-8) for its 27th edition.
entertainment.body:
It’s difficult not to be charmed, and in rather a hurry, by a city as thoroughly enamored with its musical heritage as Reykjavík. The first clue comes at 30,000 feet, with Icelandair’s in-flight playlists devoted entirely to homegrown artists. Down on terra firma, The World Of Icelandic Music, a new audio-guided exhibition downtown, charts a century-spanning journey of the country’s sounds, traversing folky beginnings and the anarcho-punk scene of the 1980s, through to the international success of Björk , Sigur Rós and contemporary jazz-pop star Laufey . “Icelandic music can stand tall and proud on its own; it’s like a brand name in itself,” Ísleifur Þórhallsson , festival manager of Iceland Airwaves and founder and CEO of Sena Live, the nation’s leading concert promoter, tells Billboard U.K. “There’s always so much good stuff to be found, the energy and variety of what you can find here is crazy. There’s always something new to discover every single year.” Perhaps it’s the near-subzero temperatures outside, or the occasional gust of wind sweeping through Reykjavík, but there’s a giddy energy about Þórhallsson when we chat in the lobby of the Parliament Hotel, which serves as a de facto meeting place for industry delegates. Dressed in an Iceland Airwaves-branded t-shirt and cap, he talks fast and fires off observations and anecdotes with gusto, as if there’s always another story waiting to be told.

The tastemaking festival and conference (Nov. 4-8) is back in town for its 27th edition, bringing together oodles of local talent and international names to offer a snapshot of a musical community whose ambition and reach continues to exceed the limitations of its size. (Iceland has a population of approximately 395,050.) Situated halfway between North America and Europe, it is also in a position to capitalize on the fast-growing market for music tourism, which Fortune Business Insights valued at $106.9 billion globally in 2025. Its national airline, Icelandair, founded Iceland Airwaves in 1999 and it remains the festival’s founding sponsor, investing heavily in the event’s marketing to attract tourists outside of the summer season.

This year, almost half of the acts booked are Icelandic, with the lineup spanning established names such as Agent Fresco , Ólöf Arnalds and underground producer Knackered , alongside an emergent generation of artists making their mark at home. They range from the dumb, sublime electroclash fun of duo Amor Vincit Omnia to Una Torfa , a folk singer-songwriter whose wistful sound recalls fellow Icelanders Of Monsters and Men , alongside freak-fried ravers SCAM , returning favourites Inspector Spacetime and RAKEL ’s pulsing, melancholic pop.

entertainment.title: KATSEYE’s Megan Performs While Sitting Due to Concussion, Sparking Fan Concern: ‘Are They Serious?’
entertainment.summary: The star told fans at the show that she was "feeling so much better."
entertainment.body:
The show must go on? With KATSEYE already down two members due to Manon and Sophia’s hiatuses, the girl group recently played a show in Austin, Texas, with Megan sitting out of the choreography — literally — as she recovers from a concussion.

As captured in clips from fans at the Wildworld Tour concert at the Moody Center on Tuesday (Nov. 10), members Yoonchae, Lara and Daniela performed their high-intensity, dance-filled set as usual. Megan, however, remained seated in a chair at the side of the stage for most of the show, wearing dark sunglasses. From there, she sang parts of the songs and occasionally grooved along to the beat, but her movement was — understandably — limited.

Regardless, the concussed star seemed determined to be a part of the show. “I’m so excited to be back on this stage,” she told concertgoers over ear-splitting screams at one point in a fan-captured clip from the show. “Thank you guys so much for showing me so much support — I’m feeling so much better.”

The modified performance came after KATSEYE canceled three shows — which had been scheduled to take place in Detroit, Chicago and Minneapolis — citing “illness” on behalf of Megan. On Nov. 5, she revealed on her Instagram Story that she’d suffered a concussion, writing that she was “devastated” and “doing everything I possibly can to recover.”

Four days later, she gave an update on Weverse , explaining that the Austin show would go on as planned, but with “reduced choreography, less intense movement and taking breaks as needed” on her end. “I won’t be going full out just yet!” she added. “My doctors have recommended these limitations for now, and I’ll need to be reassessed before returning to unrestricted performances.”

The decision to go forward with the show with Megan sitting down was polarizing among EYEKONs, many of whom expressed concern that she’d be in such a loud, overstimulating environment while dealing with a head injury. “are they serious??? why is she not FULLY on recovery this actually scares me…,” one fan commented on a video posted to X of Megan at the concert. Another person wrote on X, “This is a terrible environment for someone with a concussion. This is inhumane.”

“Katseye def doing an exposé documentary in like 10 years,” another person posted on X . “Having Megan perform like that is wild af im disgusted.”

Billboard has reached out to the girl group’s label, HYBE x Geffen, for comment.

entertainment.title: Daveigh Chase Was Found in Car With Meth Pipe Days Before Death
entertainment.summary: More details have come to light about Daveigh Chase’s heartbreaking final days. Before the Lilo & Stitch star died at 35 on June 16, she was found in the back of a car and...
entertainment.body:
More details have come to light about Daveigh Chase ’s heartbreaking final days.

Before the Lilo & Stitch star died at 35 on June 16 , she was found in the back of a car and subsequently hospitalized for various illnesses, the Los Angeles Medical Examiner confirmed to Us Weekly Nov. 10.

On June 4, the child star “was found in the back seat of a vehicle with complaints of headache, weakness, confusion, right thumb pain and a meth pipe nearby” just eight days before her death, the medical examiner told the outlet. She was then transported to a hospital by ambulance.

She was admitted with “advanced HIV/AIDS with wasting” and “cryptococcus without meningitis,” according to the medical examiner’s investigation report obtained by the outlet.

Wasting is a condition in which a person involuntarily loses at least 10 percent of their body weight, including muscle mass and fat, according to the National Cancer Institute . It often affects people with severe chronic conditions, per the Cleveland Clinic .

Meanwhile, Cryptococcus is an illness that stems from a fungal infection in the body, per the Cleveland Clinic , which noted that people with compromised immune systems—such as those with HIV/AIDS—are at a higher risk of experiencing the illness.

In addition to an infection in her thumb, Chase (real name Daveigh Schwallier ) was also diagnosed with MRSA, or Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection, at the hospital, a type of staph bacteria “that's become resistant to many of the antibiotics used to treat ordinary staph infections,” according to the Mayo Clinic .

The report also noted that toxicological screenings found Chase positive for “methamphetamine and fentanyl” in her system.

entertainment.title: Peacock Overhauls Mobile App for Vertical Video Era in Effort to “Win Another Hour Per User, Per Month”
entertainment.summary: It is Peacock's largest mobile update ever, NBCUniversal Media Group chairman Matt Strauss says.
entertainment.body:
Peacock mobile users might want to check their app store for updates — the NBCUniversal streaming platform is undergoing its largest mobile revamp ever.

Peacock mobile 2.0 (it’s probably well beyond 2.0, but stick with us here) is designed to, in part, “win another hour per user, per month,” Matt Strauss , chairman of NBCUniversal Media Group, told a small group of reporters including The Hollywood Reporter on Tuesday. Peacock has been profitable for two straight quarters now, and it’s part of Strauss’s job to keep it that way.

To accomplish that reasonable-sounding goal, NBCU is overhauling Peacock’s smartphone display and functionality for the vertical video craze, which it boasts as having been early money on, as well as the Comcast entertainment brand’s fandoms and its sports content.

Peacock users who use the app on both their TV and smartphone double the engagement of those who only sign in on their television. As John Jelley, the group’s senior vice president of product and UX (user experience), sees it, today’s opportunity is on the smaller of the two screens.

“Every streamer today is really a sea of sameness on the homepage. Because they’ve taken a TV experience and largely ported it over, they are expecting the user to do the sorting,” Jelley said. “We see an opportunity to recognize what a fan is trying to accomplish in that session and make the next most useful action easier to find.”

“We recognize that we have to start thinking of ourselves less as a streaming platform and more of an entertainment platform,” Strauss said. “How do we super serve our franchises and our fandoms where the best experience is on our app?”

One particularly cool idea is adaptive live viewing. Peacock plans to expand its live vertical video tests to The Voice live simulcasts, NCAA basketball games and, in a clear direct response to the rise of YouTube Golf, you guessed it: golf. A “dynamic video player” will switch between vertical and horizontal video playback automatically depending on the device orientation, keeping key action in frame.

NBA games will soon get the same treatment, with “easy access to player stats” and “deeper game information sitting directly underneath the live feed in a dual screen view,” the executives say.

entertainment.title: Comedy Duo Kate Berlant and John Early to Co-Host 2027 Spirit Awards
entertainment.summary: The show is set to take place March 6 at the Hollywood Palladium for a second consecutive year after moving from its longtime home on the beach in Santa Monica.
entertainment.body:
Comedy duo Kate Berlant and John Early have been tapped to co-host the 2027 Film Independent Spirit Awards .

The comedians, actors and longtime creative collaborators will serve as emcees for the 42nd edition of the awards, which honor independent storytelling across film and TV. The show is set to take place March 6 at the Hollywood Palladium for a second consecutive year after moving from its longtime home on the beach in Santa Monica.

“If there’s one thing we don’t need, it’s another predictable awards show,” said Juan Devis, president of Film Independent. “Kate and John are two of the funniest, strangest and most brilliantly unpredictable performers working today. They embody everything we love about independent storytelling: originality, fearlessness and a healthy disregard for convention. We’re excited to shake things up, break a few rules and have some fun along the way.” Related Stories Movies Two Films Share Top Jury Prize at 50th San Francisco Frameline Festival Movies Film Independent Spirit Awards Launches New Honor for Environmental-Themed Films Named After Robert Redford

Added the co-hosts in a joint statement: “We’ve always been obsessed with awards shows, and we’re so honored we get to host the coolest one. Tune in to see if we choke under pressure!”

Berlant and Early’s comedy collaborations include the sketch series 555 and the Emmy-nominated comedy special Would It Kill You to Laugh?

In addition, Berlant’s has appeared in Sorry to Bother You, Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood, Don’t Worry Darling and The Bear. She has also starred in her one-woman show KATE and her comedy specials Cinnamon in the Wind and Parmesan .

Early is known for his breakout role in the series Search Party, as well as his stand-up special Now More Than Ever. He recently made his feature directorial debut with Maddie’s Secret, in which Berlant also appears.

Nominations for the 42nd annual awards show will be announced Dec. 2. A nominees brunch will take place Jan. 9 at The London West Hollywood.

sports.title: Todd Monken: I intend for Deshaun Watson being our starting QB
sports.summary: Monken said he doesn't anticipate making a quarterback change while confirming Watson's Week 10 return.
sports.body:
Watson did not play last week after missing a pair of practices while in the concussion protocol and the team’s plans for this Sunday remained a topic of conversation because Monken declined to say who would start during a Monday press conference. Monken explained that response by saying that he wanted to talk to the team’s coaching staff before adding that he also didn’t feel a need to make a public proclamation.

“Ultimately, the full body of work , the previous eight games we had played,” Monken said. “Deshaun played pretty well. That was my intention, I just wanted to make sure to run it by my staff before I said it publicly. I don’t know why I have to say it publicly.”

Monken was asked if he will be making a quarterback determination on a weekly basis moving forward.

“I don’t look at it week-to-week and I don’t look at it as long term,” Monken said. “We’re judged each week. I am, he is, our team is. . . . I anticipate him being our starter. That’s what he’s been, he’s been our starter. . . . I have no intention of Deshaun not being our starter.”

The Texans are 5-4 heading into their game with the Texans and they have a bye in Week 11. If they are unable to stay on the right side of .500 after that break, Monken will likely field more questions about the plan for Watson moving forward.

sports.title: Rex Ryan is arrested after allegedly running over feet of pedestrians with his truck
sports.summary: No, it's not The Onion.
sports.body:
Former Jets and Bills coach and current (for now) ESPN analyst Rex Ryan has been arrested in Nashville after allegedly running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck.

Via Edward Lewis of the New York Post , the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department said that Ryan turned himself in “on six outstanding misdemeanor warrants” for “ striking two pedestrians with his pickup truck ” just on November 5.

“The pedestrians were crossing Broadway from 4th Avenue with a walk sign when the pickup truck turned right from 4th Avenue running over both victims’ feet and making contact with one of the individual’s legs,” the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department said.

“The pedestrians said the vehicle kept going, but stopped for the red light at Broadway and Representative John Lewis Way where they waved down the driver. They said he stepped out of the truck to argue with them, got back in, and drove away. They took pictures of the truck’s license plate and the driver.”

Ryan faces two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information/render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal.

Ryan became notorious in 2010 for a foot-fetish video that appeared online. He made light of the situation last month on ESPN, saying “I’m an expert in a few things. One of them is feet .”

sports.title: Miami of Ohio penalized for Patriots-style video board trickery on field goal attempt
sports.summary: At the start of this season, a former NFL analytics staffer publicized a longstanding effort by the Patriots to confuse opposing kickers with the video board behind the goal posts, showing an image of the goal posts meant to cause an optical illusion and make it harder for a kicker to put the ball t
sports.body:
Miami of Ohio found out on Tuesday night that it’s not legal in college football, either.

Just before halftime of its game against Ohio, as Ohio lined up for a field goal, the Miami video board operator put images of goal posts on the video board, in the line of the Ohio kicker’s vision, in an attempt to confuse the visiting kicker. The referee threw a flag and announced that it was unsportsmanlike conduct .

“On the previous play, there were depictions of the field goal uprights on the scoreboard. That is a foul for unsportsmanlike conduct against Miami. Half the distance to the goal, automatic first down,” the referee said.

Ohio accepted the penalty and attempted to score a touchdown with two seconds remaining in the half on the next play, but the Miami defense held, so the penalty didn’t really cost Miami. And Miami ultimately won the game 34-17, so nothing about that play ultimately had an impact on the final result.

Miami head coach Chuck Martin said after the game that he had no idea his team could get penalized for what was shown on the video board.

“We get the scoreboard penalty,” Martin said. “I didn’t even know there was such a thing.”

Many people didn’t know there was such a penalty. Now they know.

sports.title: Colts mishandled the Jonathan Taylor situation
sports.summary: When the dust settled on the trade deadline, the Colts still had running back Jonathan Taylor under contract.
sports.body:
All signs pointed to the Colts taking the best offer at 3:45 p.m. ET and processing the paperwork before the top of the hour. Whatever the best offer was.

But that’s what a functional organization would have done. The Colts currently are not.

The Giants were willing to give up a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick for Taylor. It’s unclear for now whether anyone else was willing to do better than that.

In the interim, Taylor spent two weeks not knowing what would happen. He didn’t get an assurance he wouldn’t be traded until roughly an hour before the window closed. (Even then, the leak felt more like a “last call” to interested suitors.)

The fans spent that same period of time wondering what the Colts were doing. And Taylor got only eight carries in the 42-7 loss to Jacksonville, at a time when it felt like a trade was imminent.

So what happens next for Taylor? If they try to trade him in the offseason, they won’t do better than they would have done when a contender was willing to pay a premium in an effort to win now. And if they don’t get at least as much as they could have gotten on Tuesday, will they refuse to trade him again?

Taylor could end up being stuck on the Colts during an obvious rebuild. Then, by the time it’s rebuilt (if it ever is), Taylor will be past his prime.

The simplest explanation is that the Colts slipped into dysfunction on this one. And it’s no surprise. Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon is still fairly new to the job. The G.M. has been fired. And coach Shane Steichen hopes to win enough games to have a chance to keep his job; he surely wasn’t lobbying to lose his best player.

sports.body:
The Giants called the Falcons to see whether running back Bijan Robinson was available in a trade, according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN.

That would have been a blockbuster, but it’s unsurprising that the teams didn’t make a deal. The Falcons made a big investment in Robinson this offseason, signing him to a three-year, $66.8 million contract extension, and from all accounts they view him as one of the most important pieces of their franchise.

There’s no word on what the Giants were willing to offer, or whether the Falcons engaged at all, or simply told the Giants, “Not interested.”

The Giants did make one big trade this season, acquiring J.J. McCarthy, who has played well enough for the Giants to win their first two starts and remain in first place in the NFC East. Acquiring Robinson would have been a strong sign that the Giants believe they’re serious contenders, this year. That the Giants even tried showed that coach John Harbaugh meant it when he said they’re a team trying to win now , not build for the future.

sports.title: Raiders ended up buying a third-round pick for $650,000
sports.summary: Did the Raiders get enough for Kirk Cousins?
sports.body:
Some will say no, because the Vikings were desperate to find a quarterback after Monday night’s disastrous performance from Carson Wentz. They clearly have no faith in Kyler Murray, and they weren’t ready to hand the reins to Max Brosmer. The Raiders had leverage, and it’s fair to wonder whether they maximized.

But there’s another reality to consider. The Vikings were casting a wide net. They apparently had other options. So if the Raiders had tried to put their thumb on the scale, the Vikings would have gone to a different deli — and the Raiders would have gotten nothing.

They were obviously going to pivot from Cousins to Fernando Mendoza at some point. Possibly, after the Week 13 bye against the Chargers. So they accelerated the plan and got something when they otherwise would have gotten nothing.

Along the way, they avoided the $10 million guaranteed 2027 roster bonus that was engineered to stick the Falcons with $8.7 million of Cousins’s $10 million pay for 2026. In the end, the Raiders paid half of Cousins’s $1.3 million base salary.

Setting aside the fact that they got nine games out of Cousins (including four wins) and a great mentor for Mendoza, the Raiders ultimately bought a third-round pick for $650,000.

In 2017, the Browns bought a second-round pick from the Texans for $16 million, in the form of taking on Brock Osweiler’s remaining salary guarantee under a contract Houston quickly regretted. If a second-round pick was worth $16 million then, how much is a third-round pick worth now?

So it was a win for the Raiders. And it was a win for the Vikings.

It also was a win for Cousins, who’ll now be the starter for the rest of the season in Minnesota, without having to worry about getting benched for Murray, Wentz, or Brosmer.

It’s likely that Thomas — who hasn’t played in a 2026 regular-season game — will surrender the number to Cousins. Possibly for an appropriate contribution to the charity of Thomas’s choice. Or possibly after Cousins pulls a Jared Verse and shows up for practice on Wednesday wearing No. 8.

There’s another possibility, which is as intriguing as it is unlikely. Given that Hall of Famer Fran Tarkenton, who like Cousins had a second stint as Minnesota’s starter, is very enthused by the return of Cousins, Tarkenton could offer to temporarily unretire No. 10.

I know. I know. I’ve made clear my position that retired numbers shouldn’t be unretired. More specifically, future players shouldn’t initiate the request, since it puts the player for whom the number was retired in a no-win spot. But if the idea comes from the player who holds the permanent rights to the number, that’s different.

It’s still unlikely. And it would look strange to see Cousins in No. 10. So it makes sense for him to get back in No. 8, and for Thomas to pick one of the other available numbers, like No. 9 (which he wore during his season at Tennessee) or No. 6 (which he wore before that at Middle Tennessee State).

sports.title: John Spytek: Fernando Mendoza passed every test, allowed us to make a hard decision
sports.summary: It took longer than it has for most quarterbacks drafted first overall, but Fernando Mendoza's time has come in Las Vegas.
sports.body:
Tuesday’s trade of Kirk Cousins means that Mendoza is now the No. 1 quarterback for the Raiders and he’ll make his first NFL start in Sunday’s game against the Seahawks. The Raiders went into the season determined to give Mendoza as much time as possible to learn from Cousins and their 4-5 start made it possible to stick with the plan rather than turn attention to the future.

The move would have waited a little while longer if the Vikings were not motivated buyers in the wake of Monday night’s disastrous performance against the Bills, but General Manager John Spytek said at a Tuesday press conference that the trade would not have happened without Mendoza showing the team that he’s ready.

“It’s something that he’s worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building,” Spytek said. “He passed every test. I want to stop short of saying he’s earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback.”

While the Raiders feel Mendoza is ready, it is a big change to go from the practice field to game action and the Seahawks are a tough first opponent for the rookie. The Raiders drafted Mendoza to be their leader, however, and head coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza has “exceeded those expectations” while learning from a good teacher.

“I think with the right role model that will accelerate his growth and we had, you know, we had the right role model,” Kubiak said.

Becoming the starter is just the beginning for Mendoza and it kicks off an era the Raiders hope will bring them back to the upper rungs of the AFC in the years to come.

sports.title: Fran Tarkenton raves about Kirk Cousins's return to Minnesota
sports.summary: On Monday night, I was explaining to my wife the bizarre situation in Minnesota, where a championship-caliber defense has been paired with an offense that would have trouble scoring a touchdown in the lower divisions of college football.
sports.body:
Actually, he is. And the end result to the expedited search came from the Tarkenton playbook: The Vikings brought back a former Vikings quarterback in trading with the Raiders for Kirk Cousins.

On Tuesday, Tarkenton gushed about the return of Cousins. “I think it’s the greatest thing that could have happened to us ,” Tarkenton told Darren Wolfson of KSTP. “We were lost. We were winning on defense. We had no offense. We had no quarterback. And now we’ve got Kirk coming back, who is having a great year. He’s a great player. He’s a better person than player. Our team should lift up now. And we’re in the best division in football. Our defense has kept us in the hunt.

“And having Kirk — I cannot tell you how happy I am for the Vikings, for the fans, for the Wilfs, and for all the players and the old-timers like myself. We’ve got a chance with Kirk Cousins.”

Tarkenton spent 1961 through 1966 with the Vikings before returning from 1972 through 1978. And, as it turns out, his comments about Cousins weren’t the only news he made this week.

Tarkenton apparently earned a mere $1.2 million during his entire 18-year NFL career. But that was just the starting point. He has amassed enough of a fortune in the business world to recently buy — at age 86 — a $51.89 million home in Palm Beach .

Tarkenton blazed the trail for today’s former quarterbacks who work even harder in retirement. He was the first NFL player to host Saturday Night Live , and his TV career included a co-hosting gig on That’s Incredible and a four-year stint in the Monday Night Football booth.

The big money came in the business world, specifically computer software. He also has made many millions as an early investor in Apple.

And, if you watch the clip, you’ll see that Tarkenton still has a verbal and mental fastball.

sports.title: CBA allows 49ers to not pay Brandon Aiyuk during two-week roster exemption
sports.summary: When unusual situations emerge in the NFL, it becomes a piece-by-piece exercise in figuring out the specific rules that apply.
sports.body:
He’s back on the 49ers, at a salary of $13.75 million for the rest of the season. That fact pointed to the 49ers releasing him by 4:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, in order to avoid owing him one-ninth of the total amount ($1.52 million) for Week 10.

But here’s where yet another obscure wrinkle applies. Under Article 20, Section 4 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement, the 49ers owe Aiyuk nothing during his two-week roster exemption.

From the relevant provision: “If a Club obtains a roster exemption for a player under contract who does not report to his Club at least five days before the final day of Preseason Training Camp as defined in Article 23, Section 10, the player will not be entitled to preseason or regular season compensation until such exemption is removed, provided the player is given written notice of such fact upon reporting to the Club. If such notice is not given to the player, the player must be paid his Paragraph 5 Salary during his exemption.”

So if the 49ers gave Aiyuk written notice that he won’t be paid during the two-week roster exemption (and they surely did), they don’t have to pay him. Which pushes their deadline for avoiding owing him a game check until Tuesday, November 24 — one day after the expiration of the exemption.

Why not just cut him? The 49ers are delaying the move because they can, postponing by up to two weeks his passage through waivers and, given his salary, inevitable free agency.

In the interim, he’s on the team. But Aiyuk won’t be reporting for work on Wednesday. He has been excused, we’re told, from team activities and he’s working out on his own.

The 49ers could release him at any moment. There’s no reason not to do so, other than to apply the brakes to his ability to join another team.

The circumstances counter the notion that he was reinstated by the league subject to any type of agreement with the 49ers. If that had happened, the agreement surely would have included a requirement that the 49ers promptly cut him.

sports.title: In Kirk Cousins, the Vikings landed their first choice
sports.summary: After last night's abysmal performance by the offense against the Bills, the Vikings mobilized to trade for a quarterback.
sports.body:
Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Kirk Cousins was Minnesota’s first choice.

The Vikings explored other options. Multiple players, including fellow former Vikings quarterback Daniel Jones.

Cousins’s history with the team makes it easier to get him up to speed. He had 25 regular-season games with coach Kevin O’Connell, and four seasons with receiver Justin Jefferson.

The existence of options may have helped the Vikings keep the compensation to only a third-round pick. Given the level of desperation, the Vikings seemed destined to give up more than that to fix a problem that threatened to implode the season.

That’s not an overstatement. The dam was breaking. Frustration was rampant during the debacle against the Bills, on both sides of the ball.

It was a simple proposition. If the Vikings didn’t trade for a quarterback on Tuesday, they could not be considered a serious franchise.

In the end, they managed to stop the bleeding by sending their third-round pick (their own, not the one they acquired from the Eagles for defensive end Jonathan Greenard) to the Raiders for Cousins.

It’s unclear how much better things will be with Cousins back in the fold. It can’t get worse than what they put on the field for Week 9.

sports.title: John Spytek: First "real" call on Kirk Cousins came this morning
sports.summary: As NFL trades slip into hibernation until March, it's important to remember something the next time players can be sent from one team to another.
sports.body:
Teams push plenty of BS to the media — and the media often passes it along without scrutiny.

Case in point: The internally inconsistent claim made by ESPN on Saturday, undoubtedly based on information straight from the Raiders.

“As of this weekend,” Adam Schefter of ESPN tweeted, “the Raiders had not received any trade inquiries regarding their starting quarterback Kirk Cousins, nor are they interested in dealing him , per league sources. They plan to keep sticking with him until they believe their No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is ready.”

So the Raiders hadn’t received any trade inquiries, but they weren’t interested in the trade inquiries they hadn’t received? Right.

In a press conference with reporters on Tuesday, Raiders G.M. John Spytek addressed how it all came to be.

“I never made one call on Kirk Cousins,” Spytek said. “And I got a few phone calls. But one real one this morning.”

The “real one” ultimately entailed getting a third-round pick for Cousins. Which further highlights how silly it is for a team to claim — and for the media to share — the idea that “WE’RE NOT INTERESTED.”

Everyone is interested in a trade offer for all but a small handful of players in the entire league. Anything else is posturing. And, as is often the case when it comes to NFL reporting, the insiders allow themselves to become extensions of the team’s P.R. department in an effort to send a given message.

Buffalo has agreed to acquire veteran safety Amani Hooker from Tennessee.

Tom Pelissero of Netflix was first to report the trade. Multiple reporters note Buffalo will send Tennessee a second-round pick in exchange for Hooker and a fifth-round pick.

Hooker, 28, currently leads the league with five interceptions in 2026. He’s also recorded 52 total tackles with one tackle for loss.

A fourth-round pick in the 2019 draft, Hooker has appeared in 103 games with 74 starts. He’s tallied 17 career interceptions with 45 passes defensed and five forced fumbles.

sports.title: Colts agree to trade Keenan Allen to 49ers
sports.summary: Dealing with several of injuries at the position, San Francisco is adding depth at receiver.
sports.body:
Per a joint report from ESPN and NFL Network, the Colts are trading Keenan Allen to the 49ers.

Indianapolis will receive a sixth-round pick in exchange for the veteran wideout.

Allen joined the Colts in mid-August to help that club with its receiver depth. But with Indianapolis at 2-7, the team is continuing to trade veterans for draft assets.

Allen has recorded 40 receptions for 351 yards with a touchdown so far in 2026.

Last year, he recorded 81 receptions for 777 yards with four touchdowns with the Chargers.

sports.title: Bengals call off trade for Arnold Ebiketie
sports.summary: Tuesday morning brought word that the Bengals had agreed to acquire pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie in a trade with the Eagles, but that agreement will not be finalized ahead of the 4 p.m.
sports.body:
According to multiple reports, the Bengals have called off the trade and will not be sending a 2027 sixth-round pick to Philadelphia.

The reports surfaced shortly after a tweet by OverTheCap.com contributor Nick Korte explained the compensatory pick ramifications of the deal . According to Korte, who focuses on the compensatory pick system, acquiring Ebiketie would put the Bengals in position to forfeit the third-round compensatory pick that they are currently set to receive for Trey Hendrickson leaving the team to sign with the Ravens.

That would greatly increase the price that the Bengals were going to pay to acquire Ebiketie and it appears they found it too high to move forward with the deal.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have allowed 16 total points the past two games, but the unit has certainly faced lesser competition at quarterback. How much should we take from Buffalo’s recent defensive efforts? Is it all a mirage because they faced one snap of Lamar Jackson, only a few attempts from Tyler Huntley, then Joey Fagnano, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer? Or is Buffalo really onto something defensively? These type of questions are precisely why I created Defensive Impact on Passing (DIP). I introduced the new metric a few weeks ago, and if you missed that article, here’s how I can summarize DIP — it measures how well a defense performs against opposing quarterbacks relative to how those same quarterbacks perform against other defenses on their schedule. Pretty straightforward right? Baked into DIP is the exclusion of garbage time, and, like all EPA-based defensive stats, a negative figure is better. Also, quarterbacks need at least 30 attempts against other opponents to be counted toward a defense’s DIP. Here are the full DIP rankings after Week 9: [Image: https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/DIPWeek9.png?quality=90&strip=all] You can see the Bills defense has moved all the way up to 15th in DIP. Buffalo’s unit made a steady climb after the first month or so of the season. It was 20th after Week 8 and 23rd through Week 6. And considering Buffalo’s current DIP placement, here’s where I land on what we can take from the club’s defensive efforts in Weeks 8 and 9 — for as much as the Bills defense was likely “helped” by low-level quarterback play these past two weeks it was close to equally as “hurt” by top-level quarterbacks it played in the first month-ish of the season. The analysis has to go both ways. And from that chart, you’ll notice that the DIP of the Bills defense is actually now into the negatives. sports.summary: For a while Monday night, the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings seemed to be competing to see which offense could frustrate its fans the most. sports.body: For a while Monday night, the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings seemed to be competing to see which offense could frustrate its fans the most. Neither team could get much going, and Josh Allen wasn’t doing much to hide his irritation. Playing without both his starting left tackle and left guard as Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson watched from the sidelines, Allen spent far too much time trying to escape a Minnesota defense that was coming through Buffalo’s offensive line like it had been invited. Fortunately, the Bills’ defense was giving the Vikings just as much trouble, and the scoreboard wasn’t moving much in either direction. But there’s only so long you can keep Josh Allen and the Bills’ offense quiet. Once Buffalo had a chance to figure out what Minnesota was throwing at them, the adjustments started paying off. It wasn’t the high-octane, 30-plus-point offense Bills fans have grown accustomed to watching, but it didn’t need to be. James Cook got rolling, Allen found a way to move the ball, and Tyler Bass quietly put together an 11-point night that deserves a little more attention. And let’s not forget fellow special-teams specialist Tommy Doman getting in on the tackling action. Because who doesn’t love seeing a punter-moonlighting-as-a-kicker make a tackle? By the time it was over, Buffalo had turned an aggravating start into a 23-6 win, improved to 7-1, and climbed to the top of the NFL standings. Not just the AFC East. Not just the AFC. All 32 teams. And while the offense was busy figuring things out, the defense was putting together another performance worth talking about. Three takeaways, fewer than 200 yards allowed, and a Minnesota offense that couldn’t convert a single third down. Of course, the win also came with a few entries in the record books. Josh Allen passed 5,000 career rushing yards and tied Peyton Manning’s mark of 322 total touchdowns through a player’s first 10 seasons. James Cook joined the 5,000-yard rushing club himself, giving the Bills two major career milestones in the same game. And that was just the beginning. sports.body: The Andre Cisco era is over for the New York Jets. Actually, that’s a misnomer. These days we seem to always designate something an era that in no way merits the term. Andre Cisco falls firmly in that category. The New York Jets have traded backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth round draft pick. That’s better. The Jets originally acquired Andre Cisco by signing him as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. Cisco was brought in expecting to be a playmaker in the back end of the defense, but it did not work out that way. After eight weeks of uninspired play in 2025 in which Cisco racked up zero interceptions, one pass defended, one tackle for loss and one fumble recovery, with little in the way of defensive playmaking, Cisco’s 2025 campaign ended with a season ending injury. The Jets let his contract expire in 2026 and Cisco explored free agency before the Jets brought him back on a one year, $2.2 million deal. He was expected to compete with Dane Belton for the safety spot opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick, but Belton is clearly the better player. Fitzpatrick missed time early in the season, opening up playing time for Cisco, but Cisco did little with the opportunity. Once Fitzpatrick returned to action Cisco was relegated primarily to special teams play. Over parts of two seasons Andre Cisco played 17 games for the Jets, starting 12. He racked up a total of 64 tackles, one sack, two passes defended, one forced fumble, three tackles for loss and one fumble recovery with the Jets. Cisco allowed an abysmal 115 passer rating in coverage during his time with the Jets. The trade of Cisco opens up playing time for 2025 fourth round draft pick Malachi Moore in the short run. 2026 seventh round pick V.J. Payne also stands to benefit from the trade as he works his way back from a preseason injury that has kept him out of action so far this season.
